brief: A tool caddy with a carry handle and divided bins for screws and bits.

requirements.requirement: Tool caddy structure (compact clustered base forming a portable caddy)
requirements.evidence: Three Full hex bases at 0,0,0 / 1,0,0 / 0,1,0 forming triangular cluster, locked with jointBolt:0#0,0#0 and jointBolt:0#0,0#5; meshClash clear.
handle:0,0,0;top on cover:0,0,0;full;top (requires cover, satisfied); centered for carrying.

requirements.requirement: Divided bins for screws and bits
requirements.evidence: bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments) and bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments) provide divided storage for screws and bits.

finish.summary: Tool caddy built from 3 Full hex bases in triangular cluster. Central cell has full cover with top handle for carrying; two outer cells have divided full-depth bins (div2 and div3) for screws/bits. Joint bolts lock cluster; check_build ok, meshClash clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

result.note: No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
